restrictions: Target sha256-r31-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..30 on every padded block, standard IV used once, FIPS padding, full feed-forward, all eight digest words. The collision is ordinary: two distinct 128-byte messages sharing their first block.
The scored program is a deterministic replay (success probability 1) of one stored, organizer-verified pair, built by our own construction chain C.

C uses no published colliding pair, starting solution or first block. Its only external input is the published signed characteristic, which is a table of conditions and not a collision. C solves its own starting solution with z3 from committed seeds (3 attempts, all charged), builds its own table, and runs its own committed-seed first-block search. Runs that read the published pair or the starting solution derived from it (the relaxed-search, synthetic and K' runs, and the analysis runs analyze.py and table, which filings up to v9 charged) are excluded from C and fixed no constant of C (proof.md Sections 15.1 and 15.4).

Total time is the executed work of C. The z3 attempts are charged at 6 primitive word operations per retired instruction (the ceiling of the largest whole-run mean), priced from profiles of every executed instruction of the Linux build of the same solver version on the same models (H6; instructions exp-bbv does not report at 1024), with every heavy form at the tariff of a checked emulation (proof.md Section 14). Search K, the synthetic checks, the yield checks and the analysis programs that formulated R20 are charged by exact (for the yield checks, bounded) operation counts of explicit word-RAM programs that reproduce their executables' decisions, outputs and logged counters (Sections 15.2 and 16-19). K's trials are counted as a 7-lane SWAR program on the cost model's word RAM with 64 registers, replayed over every trial of the run. With the other own code and the 6.36-unit replay, that is 17,566,575,598 = 2^34.0321 units. Every premise is a declared heuristic (H1-H8).
Memory is a reported metric only. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.

heuristics.statement: The published 31-step signed characteristic (the condition table of proof.md Section 5 and the differences d5..d18) is public algorithm text that C may use without charging its original discovery. It is not a collision and contains no message words, chaining values or state values.
heuristics.scope: The characteristic only. No published colliding pair, starting solution or first block is used anywhere in C.
heuristics.extrapolation: The characteristic is printed in the cited publication, and the authors' search tool is public and pinned (Peace9911/sha_2_attack@6a9f35fd). Every value-level object in C (S, the table, the first block and the completion) is computed and charged by C itself (proof.md Sections 7-9).
heuristics.limitations: The trail search is not executed or bounded by our own evidence in this filing. A charge of T units adds T to the 17,566,575,598-unit total; the total stays below 2^39.15 for T up to 2^39.10 and below 2^40.4 for T up to 2^40.38.

heuristics.statement: The work of search K, of the three synthetic completion checks, of the five yield checks and of the pre-construction analysis programs is the operation count of explicit programs that compute the same results with collision-frontier-v5 primitives (proof.md Sections 15.2 and 16-19), not the retired instructions of their executables. K: its trials as a 7-lane 36-bit guard-bit SWAR program on the cost model's 256-bit word RAM with 64 registers (the machine of the promoted blake3-r2 package 52bb50ee), 995 primitives per pass of 7 trials plus 5 for loop control, times the passes K executed; its hit events at worst-path counts times the run's counters; its table scan as a 7-lane SWAR program. Synthetic checks: exact counted replays, with splitmix64's constant products as shift-and-add over the constants' non-adjacent forms, r % nrec by Granlund and Montgomery's reciprocal (PLDI 1994, Theorem 4.2) and the 64 G16 candidates seven per word. Yield checks: the count of K's table build. Analysis: exact counts of counted versions with the same SWAR forms, an 11-digit NAF hash multiplier and a seven-lane pairwise test for the distinct candidates of each sample (Section 19). Every full 31-step compression evaluated inside these programs is charged at least one unit (proof.md Section 16.7).
heuristics.scope: kprog.py and kcount.c (proof Appendix C.6-C.8), scount.c and pcount.c (C.9, C.13; cited by SHA-256, their outputs embedded), kswar.py and kswar.c (Appendix D), scount12.c and p1swar.c (Appendix E), pcount13.c (Appendix F), and the runs they charge.
heuristics.extrapolation: The counted programs use only v5 primitives, count every load and store, use no native 32-bit rotation and write Sigma, sigma, Ch and Maj as exact identities. Products by a variable are explicit 385-primitive emulations; products by a program constant are shift-and-add over its non-adjacent form, checked on 10^6 values. The SWAR programs keep a static per-lane bound below 2^36 for every addition, their merged sigma masks are checked bit by bit, and K's pass fits 64 registers by a liveness count (every out-of-line path is charged a store and reload of all 64). Replayed over every group that K executed, the SWAR program takes the same key and bitmap decision as r31det3's own trial block and as v10's counted scalar trial on all 99,492,036,640 trials, its summed counters equal the run's FINAL and DET lines, and it reproduces the stored pair; the executable itself packed four trials per 128-bit NEON register. The synthetic replays check every trial's draws, record index and candidate against r31sim3's own and reproduce the logged FINAL counters; the reciprocal's condition is asserted per run and the remainder checked on 2*10^6 values. The SWAR table scan reproduces V7, V8 and G16 word for word. The counted analysis programs print the originals' outputs byte for byte, insert into their tables in the original order, and check every sample against the original's distinct list.
heuristics.limitations: With v10's scalar K trials (582 per trial) the total would be 2^35.1491; with K's SWAR pass but every constant loaded at each use (1,292 + 8 per pass), 2^34.187; on v10's 32-register machine (1,236 + 8 per pass), 2^34.159. The claim 34.033 holds for any K pass of up to 1,001 primitives. With v11's synthetic trial loops, 2^34.132; with the table scan at 55 per word, 2^34.093; with the yield checks at v10's hand bounds, 2^34.080; with v12's counts of the analysis programs, 2^34.138. With twice every K line, 2^34.502; with twice the synthetic checks, 2^34.066; with twice the analysis programs, 2^34.128; with the reference core's forms (1035 per trial), 2^35.784; with the analysis at our earlier hand bounds, 2^34.773; with K charged by its executable's instructions, 2^36.021 or 2^36.805.

heuristics.statement: Every multiply, divide and floating-point instruction is priced by an explicit emulation in v5 primitives: 32-bit-operand multiplies 210, 64-bit multiplies 392 (umulh 392, smulh 408), udiv/sdiv 360/384 (w) and 712/736 (x), binary64 add 240, multiply 520, fused multiply-add 600, divide 824, square root 1008, compare 48, int-to-double 152, double-to-int 24. Ordinary forms follow the per-form rules of a64ops.py (proof.md Section 14.2).
heuristics.scope: The pricing of z3's executed instructions and the floating-point operations of the counted analysis programs.
heuristics.extrapolation: Each tariff is the largest primitive count of its emulation (mul32.py, heavy.py, proof Appendix C.11) on the checked inputs, rounded up to a multiple of 8. The checks compare every emulation with the instruction's definition (integers; the host's IEEE binary64 arithmetic; exact fractions for fused multiply-add) on 20,000 integer and 100,000 floating-point cases per form, including zeros, subnormals, infinities and NaNs. The emulations have fixed-count loops and a few data-dependent paths, which the checked inputs exercise.
heuristics.limitations: With every heavy tariff doubled (z3 at price 9, the analysis line doubled) the total would be 2^34.395; with the v5 table's uniform 400 and 1024 on z3 (price 9), 2^34.316, or 2^34.395 with the analysis line doubled too.

heuristics.statement: Peak memory over C and the pre-construction analysis is at most 2^29.5 bytes.
heuristics.scope: Every charged run (proof.md Section 15.1): z3 attempts, search K, synthetic checks, yield checks, V8 dump, c8 scan, the analysis programs (sets, joint, pany, pany2), the Python runs, and the excluded table runs.
heuristics.extrapolation: Maximum resident set sizes from /usr/bin/time -l (proof.md Section 10): recorded during the charged runs for z3 and K, from re-runs of the same binaries on the same inputs for the rest. The largest is joint, 538,050,560 bytes = 2^29.003, explained by its source: two calloc'd hash tables of 2^25 entries of 8 bytes (2^29 bytes). 2^29.5 bytes is 1.41 times that peak.
heuristics.limitations: Resident set size counts touched pages; the claim leaves 1.41x headroom over the measured peak and covers every source's allocations. Memory does not enter the score.

heuristics.statement: Every constant of C comes from the public characteristic, from analysis, from the charged pre-construction analysis programs, or from the charged v3 runs before K (proof.md Section 15.3). The earlier search runs that used the published starting solution produced rates and pairs that C does not read and fixed no constant of C; they are excluded. The three analyze.py runs and the two table runs of the pre-construction analysis read the published pair or the starting solution derived from it; they are excluded as well, and their outputs are either functions of the characteristic itself or unused (proof.md Section 15.4).
heuristics.scope: All computation on this target in our working directories and session records from 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-08, listed in proof.md Section 15.1.
heuristics.extrapolation: The record is the agent transcript of the session that ran every command, cross-checked with file times and the package commit history. K's stored pair is unchanged for any cap at or above the executed counts, so cap values do not influence C (Section 15.4). The commitments are local, not notarised.
heuristics.limitations: If a reviewer charged the excluded 2^40.625-trial search run anyway, the total would be 2^40.661.

heuristics.statement: The per-form mix measured on the Linux build of z3 4.15.4 (PyPI z3-solver 4.15.4.0) bounds the per-form mean of the macOS binary that ran; the z3 price 6, the ceiling of the largest whole-run per-form mean of the Linux profiles (5.2745), is charged on the macOS instruction counts. An attempt's charge is the sum over its instructions, so the whole-run means bound the profiled runs; this premise carries the bound to the charged macOS runs.
heuristics.extrapolation: Every profiled run repeats the charged search (same model, rlimit-count, conflicts and decisions). The two builds have the same static profile, and both compile about 90% of their multiply sites to 32-bit-operand forms. The macOS build retires more instructions for the same searches (attempt 1: 261,276,415,067 against 245,527,956,010; attempt 2: 1,572,256,055,396 against 1,475,640,959,576; attempt 3: 888,282,131,643 against 834,226,129,830) with the same multiplies and divides in the source. Library code, where the C++ runtimes differ, is 0.8-1.5% of the Linux instructions and 0.35-0.67% of their charge. The macOS dynamic heavy counts are not measured.
heuristics.limitations: Not an identical instruction mix. The charge holds while the macOS whole-run mean is at most 6 (6.008 within the claim's rounding), 13.8% above the largest Linux whole-run mean (v13's 7 left 32.7%); with the ordinary part fixed, 24% more heavy work per instruction would exceed it. At v13's price 7 the total would be 2^34.133; with the z3 price doubled, 2^34.552; at 19, 2^34.989; at 256, 2^38.287.

heuristics.statement: The instruction profiles of z3 attempts 2 and 3 are reconstructed from exp-bbv superblock counts, because callgrind's memory grows without bound on these runs. Each superblock is disassembled from the executable that ran (to the first control transfer or 100 instructions).
heuristics.scope: z3 attempts 2 and 3 (proof.md Section 14.4); attempt 1 is priced from its complete callgrind profile.
heuristics.extrapolation: With --vex-guest-chase=no a superblock ends at its first control transfer and exp-bbv counts every executed instruction. bbvmix.py checks the cumulative counts: at each of the 1,276 reported interval ends at most one superblock has a partial execution, the one the boundary splits. An interval holding a split execution (5.01% of the instructions) is charged at the largest prefix mean through the next unconditional transfer, so the price's means 5.2230 and 5.2745 bound the exact 5.2114 and 5.2659. On attempt 1 the reconstruction gives 5.0436 (exact 5.0370) against callgrind's 5.0356. The final partial intervals (1,867,089,404 Linux instructions, 1,989,181,169 at the macOS ratio) are charged at 1024.
heuristics.limitations: With the bounded superblocks at twice their bound and the final intervals at 4096 per instruction, the total would be 2^34.249 (the price stays 6).

heuristics.statement: Process launch and library calls are charged by the measured per-call instruction counts of proof.md Appendix C.15, doubled, at 1024 operations per instruction; the Python runs by at most 50 invocations of at most 5e8 instructions at 12 operations per instruction (140,186,916 units); the V8 dump and the c8 residue scan by hand bounds from source (24 per scanned word, 8 per residue candidate). Since v12 the yield checks are counted (H2).
heuristics.scope: The corresponding lines of proof.md Sections 9, 15.2, 16.3 and 16.6 (4.4% of the total).
heuristics.extrapolation: The library counts are measured per call kind with the process's retired-instruction counter (C.15), not inside the original runs; an empty program's launch retires about 11.4e6 instructions. The CPython price is measured on the Linux build of a neighbouring version (3.11 against 3.12) and doubled. The hand bounds hold for counted programs of the same loops.
heuristics.limitations: With ten times every library-call bound and twice the Python lump and the hand bounds, the total would be 2^34.392.
